highlights: Questions and approvals now open in an Agentry card window instead of your system's message box.
No has the focus when a card opens, so Enter or Escape never says yes by accident.
Settings, Coding tools: see which coding tools are on this computer, their desktop apps included, without running them.
Install the Agentry plugin into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, pi, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI and more, with one click each.
Each install shows you the tool's exact commands first, and runs them only after you say yes.
A schedule on a runhost changes model from its card, and Recent runs names the runhost a run ran on.
The Assistant can have the Drafter revise one of your QuickAgents, In Agentry or on this computer, asking you first.
It can make one private, retire or restore it, yank a version or withdraw one held for review, asking each time.
It reads a QuickAgent it fetched or revised in the same reply, and a failed fork now says why it failed.
Your computer's library: presets fill in their optional settings, and an open port alone no longer counts as installed.
The Assistant can list the QuickAgents you publish, say where each version stands, and copy one to work on.
It can fork a public QuickAgent, submit new versions, and create new private ones, asking you each time.
Before a submission, Agentry shows you the files and the capabilities that changed, and who receives it.
Your organization's managed settings now also hold runs In Agentry, bug reports and the choices in Settings.
Settings shows each security setting your organization manages: Managed by it with a padlock, or Set by it as a default.
A schedule held by your organization's managed settings says so on its row, and Run now tells you why.
When the registry rotates its signing key with a handover from your pinned key, Agentry trusts the new key itself.
Settings → Models keeps up to ten saved models, each a provider and a model, with your default starred.
Pick the model when a run starts, for each schedule and for each agent, the one on Home included.
Make a saved model available on a runhost, checked there, and put that runhost's agents on it.
A model whose key or sign-in is missing is greyed with the fix, and nothing falls back to your default.
Your computer lists your own applications: add any, from the library or by hand, and approve its server or its windows.
A QuickAgent names an application by id: Agentry Desktop uses yours with that id, or lets you choose one and remembers.
A tool nobody has classed asks you before each call; class it read or act on its card and it asks no more.
A run's receipt says whether each application came from the library or from you, and counts its calls.
If your organization's managed settings forbid Unsafe Mode, its switch stays off and Settings says who set it.
Browse shows every result: Show more brings the next thirty, and the count says how many there are.
After Skip, Home lists what is left to set up, and each item opens the step it needs.
Where runs happen has one set of names everywhere: This computer, A runhost and In Agentry.
The sidebar is grouped like Settings: Agents, Scheduled, Build, Library and Plugins, under Home.
Meeting notes and Computer use now live under Plugins, and each persistent agent is listed under Agents.
Settings has eight sections instead of fifteen, so the settings that belong together sit together.
The Assistant can run your installed QuickAgents without asking each time, once you switch that on in Settings.
Browse and the welcome say what a published version carries: a public report of its scan and its signature.
A persistent agent such as the Assistant can use Blender or Unreal Engine on your computer once you switch each on.
Switches take effect at the agent's next turn; opening or closing the application restarts nothing.
An agent on your runhost reaches the applications here while Agentry Desktop runs; Settings shows it as linked.
The Voice Writer and the Report Designer can run in the background, in a card in the corner, like a QuickAgent's run.
Every run, draft, review and build shows the same Run log, with its time, turns and tokens as it goes.
Recent runs keeps a built-in agent's log and why it failed, as it does for a QuickAgent's run.
A persistent agent's page lists its five newest subagent runs; See more… opens all of them in a card.
A QuickAgent that uses an application on your computer can now run on one of your runhosts from the run setup.
The app answers the run's use of your computer while it runs; if you close the app, the run's later calls are refused.
Computer use works on macOS and Windows too; on macOS, turning it on asks for the permissions it needs.
On Windows, Ctrl+Shift+F12 stops it, and an application run as administrator is refused: Windows blocks input to it.
QuickAgents can use Unreal Engine on your computer through Epic's own Unreal MCP plugin.
Build offers the applications on your computer a QuickAgent uses, with each one's tools and what the install will ask.
QuickAgents can see and use the windows of the applications they name on Linux, once you turn computer use on.
The tray, a banner and Ctrl+Shift+Escape pause or stop it; Keep what the agent saw saves each screenshot.
Design with AI from a document keeps its logo and its cover page's artwork, and can model the cover on yours.
The result says what it took from your document: the logo, a cover image or a cover like your cover page.
QuickAgents can use Blender on your computer: Agentry Desktop starts its MCP server and asks before code runs.
Settings → Your computer shows each application's state, the runs using it, and Pause and Stop.
Model setup shows the context window of a model on a server of your own, asked from the server or typed in.
Get models fills it in for LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp and vLLM, and Ask the server asks again.
Design with AI In Agentry can start from a document too: one PDF or Word document, uploaded for the run.
The Report Designer takes the document's colours, faces, header, footer and logo, at the same 20 credits.
Design with AI can start from a document: one PDF or Word document that already looks the way you want.
The Report Designer takes its colours, faces, header, footer and logo from it, on this computer.
The document is read in full and kept only for the run.
Design with AI in Settings → Report design writes a design, or a custom cover page, from your brief.
Run it In Agentry for 20 credits, refunded if nothing is saved, or on this computer with your own model.
What it makes is a new design, never your default: Use makes it so.
A run on your own model server summarizes and goes on when the server says the conversation is too long.
A reminder from one of the Assistant's tasks is now a message from it in the chat, not hidden in the task's folded line.
The task's notification shows that reminder as it comes.
Render in Settings → Report design now draws your design's own cover page, the cover a run's PDF opens with.
A cover of your own that cannot be drawn still falls back to the built-in band cover, and Render says so.
Render in Settings → Report design lays a sample report out in your design on this computer and shows the real pages.
It goes through the same export a run's PDF goes through, works offline, and includes changes you have not saved.
A design whose own cover cannot be drawn says so, and shows the built-in cover a run's PDF would use in its place.
Settings → Report design is a library of up to ten designs, each a brand with a header, a footer and a cover page.
Start a design from one of ten kits, then set its brand, two colours, fonts, header and footer slots and cover style.
Brand from logo offers your logo's two colours as the accent and the secondary; a cover image fills a plate cover.
Pick the design a run's PDFs take in the run's setup, here or In Agentry; your default is preselected.
You never stop a persistent agent to change it: its mail, calendar and other settings reach it at its next turn.
Update installs a running agent's new version beside it, and it moves to it at its next turn.
Disable, Uninstall and Reset stop the agent themselves, even when another app runs it.
A change the agent could not start with shows on its card as Not applied, with why.
Home starts from where your runs go: this computer, your runhost or Agentry, with the cards that place needs.
Get started on Home lists what your setup still needs, each with the button that does it.
Shortcuts on Home open Run, Draft, Create knowledge, Meeting notes, Writing Voice, Persistent agent and Setup.
Finishing setup now lands you on Home, ready to start.
Settings → Runhosts lists each runhost's persistent agents, with Start and Stop.
Talk to an agent on your runhost from its card: it answers there, on the runhost's own model.
Meeting notes' settings are above your meetings on its page, and in Settings → Meeting notes too.
Turn on Tell speakers apart on calls, and a call's transcript says Speaker 1, 2 and so on for the others.
The voices on a call are told apart on this computer after transcription; you stay Me.
Schedule a QuickAgent on your runhost: choose it and Later or Repeat in the run's setup; it runs with nobody here.
Settings → Runhosts lists each runhost's schedules and what they keep there, and removes them.
Runs of your runhost's schedules are collected when this app reaches it, and show on Home.
A persistent agent whose stored conversation is gone, as after a stop before its first message, starts on a new one.
After each update of the app, your runhosts are brought to its CLI; Settings → Runhosts shows how each went.
Pair another computer of yours with a runhost from Settings → Runhosts, or unpair this one.
A runhost can be Fedora, or RHEL, AlmaLinux or Rocky Linux, as well as Debian or Ubuntu.
A runhost can pay for its runs with your Agentry credits: Use my credits at its Model step or in Settings → Runhosts.
Revoke a runhost's credits token from Settings → Runhosts whenever you like.
Set up a Linux server of yours as a remote runhost from the first-run wizard or Settings → Runhosts.
A QuickAgent can run on your runhost: choose it in the run's setup, and the result says where it ran.
Sign a runhost in to your Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot plan from your browser, and turn its Unsafe Mode on or off.
The Assistant and the Coding agent start again with Brave Search or Fastmail on; 0.7.2 refused them.
Setup now says what it is preparing, and the Claude sign-in shows each step instead of waiting in the browser.
Claude Code and Codex are built from their newest releases, checked against each vendor's signature.
Runs on this computer get 30 minutes and no turn limit by default; set limits in Settings, Run defaults.
Build makes an agent that stays running, and installs it here as a persistent agent once it passes.
Install a persistent agent from its page in Browse, with one consent that names everything it is given.
Installed agents sit beside the built-in ones in Settings and the sidebar, with Update and Uninstall.
An agent's page lists the runs it started of its subagents, each opening the run's own page.
Starting a fourth persistent agent warns first: each one runs its own containers.
The desktop app, the CLI, the MCP server and the Agentry server now share one version, 0.7.0.
The app is built on CLI 0.7.0, so what it runs on your computer uses that release.
A Notifications page behind the bell lists what finished while you were elsewhere, with your account's notifications.
Your computer tells you when something you started finishes, unless the result is already in front of you.
A run that fails explains itself: the class, the cause, the kept log, Run again.
The run panel keeps your answers while you set up an engine or a provider in place.
Your personal agent reads how a QuickAgent wants to run: its questions, the files it takes and its guide.
Ask it to run a QuickAgent on a repository and it gives the address; Agentry fetches it, no download needed.
Before a run that fetches from a new address, Agentry asks you first.
Agentry Desktop now runs on Wails 3 with GTK 4 on Linux: Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and Fedora 44 or later.
Agents run on the newest runtime images.
Meeting notes use a rebuilt transcriber.
After Agentry Desktop moves to a newer version, What's new shows what each version since your last one brings.
Update settings has a What's new button, so you can read the newest versions' highlights again.
A persistent agent's page has a View menu with five views: Terminal, Compact, Chat, Focus and Workspace.
Agentry Desktop remembers the view you choose and uses it for every agent.
The Compact view fits more of the conversation on screen.
